title: Tailwind v4 setup
summary: Compile utility classes into a stylesheet that your page can load.
points: This course uses Tailwind CSS v4. Install a supported Node.js version and npm before using the CLI starter.
Install tailwindcss@4 and @tailwindcss/cli@4 in your own project. The CLI is a separate package.
Import tailwindcss from the input CSS file, then run the CLI with input and output paths.
Link the generated output stylesheet in HTML. Watch mode rebuilds after source changes; a production build should finish and exit.
The Play CDN is for development experiments, not the production workflow taught here. Do not mix v3 setup instructions into this v4 project.
output: The CLI scans source classes and writes output.css. The HTML must link that file. Keep source edits in input.css and HTML rather than modifying generated output.
mistake: The old tailwindcss init command and @tailwind base/components/utilities directives are not this v4 CLI setup.
challenge: Unzip the starter, install its dependencies, run the build, and open index.html. Change a utility, rebuild, and verify the visible result.

title: Utility classes & spacing
summary: Use small classes while still reasoning in CSS properties.
points: Utilities map to focused CSS declarations. Understand the underlying property before combining classes.
p-4 adds padding; m-4 adds margin; gap-4 adds space between flex or grid items. These are not interchangeable.
Numeric spacing utilities use the theme spacing value. With the default theme, 4 steps are 1rem; customized themes can differ.
Preflight supplies base styles and removes some browser defaults. Headings still need intentional typography classes.
Do not place conflicting utilities on the same element and expect the last class in the HTML attribute to win. CSS generation and cascade decide.

title: Type, color & borders
summary: Make a small visual system from intentional utility combinations.
points: text-lg changes font size; text-slate-800 changes color. Similar prefixes can represent different CSS properties.
Use font-semibold for weight, leading-relaxed for line height, and max-w-prose for a reading measure.
Headings retain semantic meaning even when Preflight removes their default browser appearance.
A border needs a width and a suitable color. Choose colors that remain distinct from the surface.
Check contrast for normal, hover, focus, and dark states. Palette names do not guarantee accessible combinations.

output: The heading is larger and heavier than the supporting paragraph. The surrounding section still needs an appropriate place in the document hierarchy.
mistake: A utility class that makes text look like a heading does not make a div a semantic heading.
challenge: Give your planner three text styles and two surfaces. Check contrast for the exact pairs you used and keep task status readable without color.

title: Flex & Grid utilities
summary: Choose the layout model first, then its utilities.
points: flex makes direct children flex items; grid makes them grid items. Layout utilities belong on the relevant container.
items-center aligns on the cross axis in Flexbox; justify-between distributes along its main axis.
grid-cols-2 creates two equal tracks; gap-4 adds gutters. Add responsive variants when columns should change.
flex-wrap permits wrapping. min-w-0 on an item can help long content shrink, while text still needs suitable wrapping.
Avoid using order utilities to create a visual sequence that disagrees with keyboard or reading order.

title: Responsive variants
summary: Unprefixed classes are the base; breakpoints add wider-screen behavior.
points: Tailwind’s default breakpoint variants use minimum widths. sm: is not a “phones only” selector.
An unprefixed class applies by default at every width unless another matching rule overrides the same property.
With the default theme, md starts at 48rem. Custom themes can change breakpoints.
Keep the viewport meta tag in the page. Test content and zoom rather than relying only on device presets.
Use complete classes such as md:grid-cols-2. Responsive variants can change layout, spacing, typography, and more.

mistake: Using only sm:text-sm does not set the smallest-screen text size. Put the base size in an unprefixed utility.
challenge: Resize your planner through the breakpoint slowly. Confirm that controls remain reachable and long task titles do not cause page overflow.

title: Interactive states
summary: Describe visual feedback without losing native behavior.
points: hover:, focus-visible:, and disabled: apply a utility only when their state condition matches.
A focus-visible outline should be easy to distinguish from the surface. Do not remove it just to simplify a design.
disabled: styles an actual disabled state; it does not disable a control by itself.
group-hover: can respond to a parent marked group; peer variants can respond to a preceding sibling marked peer.
motion-reduce: can remove nonessential transitions. Tailwind classes do not implement click handlers, storage, or form submission logic.
code:
<button type="button" disabled
  class="rounded-lg bg-rose-700 px-4 py-2 text-white
  hover:bg-rose-800 focus-visible:outline-2
  focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-rose-900
  disabled:opacity-50">Saving comes later</button>
output: This button is natively disabled, so it cannot submit or run an action. The classes describe appearance for states; they do not supply behavior.
mistake: Changing opacity does not disable a control. Likewise a hover style does not provide keyboard focus feedback.
challenge: Add visible keyboard focus to the planner’s real links. Include an honest disabled prototype action and explain why it is disabled.

title: Theme variables in v4
summary: Define shared design choices in the CSS theme.
points: In Tailwind v4, @theme declares theme variables used to generate matching utilities.
A variable in the --color-* namespace can support color utilities such as bg-brand and text-brand.
Ordinary :root custom properties are useful too, but do not automatically create new Tailwind utilities.
Keep a small palette and spacing system. Use arbitrary values only when a deliberate exception needs them.
Theme changes can affect many components. Recheck text contrast, focus outlines, and responsive behavior after changing shared values.
output: Tailwind can generate bg-paper and text-brand when it detects those complete class names in source files. Both refer to the declared theme values.
mistake: Putting --color-brand only inside :root does not register a new Tailwind theme utility.
challenge: Replace repeated palette choices with two named theme colors. Build the stylesheet and inspect the compiled result and rendered contrast.

title: Dark mode
summary: Design a second set of readable color relationships.
points: By default, dark: follows the system prefers-color-scheme setting. You do not need a custom toggle to use that default.
Pair background, foreground, border, and focus colors in each mode. Changing only the background can make text unreadable.
A manual selector strategy needs an explicit custom dark variant and behavior to set that selector. A class name alone is not a toggle.
The phase-two starter uses the system preference, so no nonworking toggle is shown.
Test both modes, including controls and muted text. Dark mode is not a substitute for contrast checks.

title: Source detection & builds
summary: Make sure the classes you use become CSS in the final file.
points: Tailwind scans source text for complete class names. It does not run JavaScript to understand string concatenation.
Keep full class names visible, such as bg-rose-700, rather than assembling fragments like bg- plus a variable.
In v4, @source can register files outside the usual detected sources. Paths are relative to the stylesheet.
Watch builds are for editing. A release build should generate the final stylesheet once, usually with minification.
Test the compiled output with the intended HTML. A development preview working does not prove the packaged output includes every needed style.
output: This explicit source configuration scans the starter’s index.html instead of unrelated folders. The finished HTML still links output.css.
mistake: Do not edit generated output.css as your source of truth; rebuilding replaces it. Change the input file or source classes.
challenge: Run a one-time minified build. Move the built HTML and output.css together to another local folder and verify the styles still load.

title: Rebuild your planner
summary: Compare two styling approaches through the same useful project.
points: Reuse your planner’s semantic structure and rewrite its presentation with Tailwind utilities.
Include a responsive grid, a wrapping toolbar, a consistent theme, and clear keyboard focus.
Use system dark-mode variants and verify both color schemes. Do not promise a custom toggle or task storage in this static phase.
Build the stylesheet from complete source classes and confirm the final HTML links the generated file.
Write a short comparison with your plain CSS version: readability, reuse, build steps, and maintenance tradeoffs.
Keep source files and setup instructions in version control. Finish the self-review before marking the project complete.
code:
# In the downloaded starter folder
npm install
npm run build
# Open index.html after the build.
# While editing, use npm run dev.

# Review: keyboard, narrow width, zoom, both color schemes
output: The starter ships with a compiled stylesheet and build instructions. Dependencies are installed only when you rebuild. Quizzes assess recall; project review remains your own practical check.
mistake: Copying every class without understanding it makes later changes harder. Explain the CSS concept behind each layout choice.
challenge: Finish the README checklist, compare screenshots with your CSS version, and explain one tradeoff you would make differently next time.
